t: For an additional amount for “Construction, Major Projects”, $207,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2017, for renovations and repairs as a consequence of damage caused by Hurricane Sandy: Provided, That none of these funds shall be available for obligation until the Secretary of Veterans Affairs submits to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate a detailed expenditure plan for funds provided under this heading: Provided further, That notwithstanding any other provision of law, such funds may be obligated and expended to carry out planning and design and major medical facility construction not otherwise authorized by law: Provided further, That such amount is designated by the Congress as being for an emergency requirement pursuant to section 251(b)(2)(A)(i) of the Balanced Budget and Emergency Deficit Control Act of 1985.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that requiring the Secretary to submit an expenditure plan before funds can be obligated is a form of consultation. But the plan goes only to congressional appropriations committees, which are inside the federal government. The section is otherwise an appropriation for Hurricane Sandy repairs and involves no state, local, public, or other outside party in any federal decision.
fable.s: none of these funds shall be available for obligation until the Secretary of Veterans Affairs submits to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate a detailed expenditure plan for funds provided under this heading

opus.w: The only procedural step here is that the Secretary of Veterans Affairs must send an expenditure plan to the House and Senate Appropriations Committees before the money can be spent. That looks like a check on the decision, but it is a report to Congress, which is part of the federal government. The section involves no states, tribes, outside experts, members of the public, comment period, hearing, or right to sue, so it is not participation.
opus.s: none of these funds shall be available for obligation until the Secretary of Veterans Affairs submits to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate a detailed expenditure plan for funds provided under this heading

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to submit a plan to congressional committees before obligating funds. Since Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, this interaction is intra-governmental and does not involve consultation or coordination with parties outside the federal government. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: Provided, That none of these funds shall be available for obligation until the Secretary of Veterans Affairs submits to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate a detailed expenditure plan for funds provided under this heading
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement to submit a plan to Congress involves "participation" because it is a procedural step before funds can be used. However, Congress is part of the federal government (inside the boundary), so reporting to or consulting with Congress is intra-governmental coordination, not participation with outside parties.
